issues.description: Key acceptance policy is complected with widget lifecycle inside keyPressEvent
issues.detail: The 'should Enter accept?' decision is a value — a small predicate over (key, config) — but it's tangled into the widget's event handler alongside hide(), item lookup, and re-dispatch to textedit. Pull the policy out as a pure function (accepts_completion(key, config)) so the widget just asks a value. Right now state, behavior, and policy share one branch.

issues.description: Branch reads config on every keypress instead of treating it as a value
issues.detail: get_conf is called inside keyPressEvent on every key, complecting configuration-read time with key-handling time. The config is a value that changes rarely; cache it on the widget and update via a signal. This separates 'what is the current policy' (value/identity) from 'a key arrived' (event), which is the time-confusion Hickey warns about.

issues.description: Negated boolean with 'not ... and not key ==' obscures the actual predicate
issues.detail: 'not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab' forces the reader to invert twice to recover the intent: 'Enter-accept is disabled AND this key is not Tab'. Name the predicate (enter_accept_disabled, is_tab) or write 'key != Qt.Key_Tab'. The logic isn't wrong, but the shape hides the rule it encodes.

issues.description: Behavior for non-Enter, non-Tab keys in this branch is unspecified by the name
issues.detail: The option is called 'use_enter_for_completions', but the new branch fires for any key that isn't Tab — including arrows, Escape, printable characters. That may be intentional (hide and forward), but the predicate's name promises 'Enter' while the code says 'not Tab'. Either rename the config or narrow the branch to the Enter keys explicitly.

issues.description: Grid-row renumbering by hand is incidental complexity from a place-oriented layout
issues.detail: Adding one row required editing four (row, col) tuples. The layout is a value (an ordered list of widgets) being expressed as mutable coordinates. Not worth fixing in this PR, but it's the kind of incidental coupling that turns a one-line feature into a four-line diff and invites off-by-one mistakes on the next insertion.

review.summary: The feature is small and the intent is right, but the implementation complects three things in one keyPressEvent branch: the policy (is Enter an accept key?), the config read (when do we learn the policy?), and the widget action (hide and forward). Pulling the policy out as a pure predicate over (key, config) and caching the config value on the widget would make this SIMPLE rather than just EASY. The double-negative condition and the name/behavior mismatch ('use_enter' vs 'not Tab') are smaller readability issues that fall out of the same lack of decomposition. The confpage row renumbering is INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY from the grid layout, not this PR's fault, but worth naming. The question that should have been asked first: what is the value here — a key-to-action map — and where should it live?
